drug_class: Topical Analgesic (Pain Reliever applied to the skin)
purpose: This combination medication is applied to the skin to help relieve minor aches and pains in muscles and joints. It is commonly used for conditions like arthritis, back pain, sprains, and sore muscles. Think of it as a medicated rub that helps soothe painful areas right where you need it.
how_it_works: Each ingredient works in a slightly different way to reduce pain. Menthol and camphor create a cooling then warming sensation on your skin, which distracts your brain from feeling deep pain — almost like a gentle trick on your nerves. Capsaicin, which comes from hot peppers, works by temporarily reducing a pain signal chemical in your nerve endings, so over time those nerves send fewer pain messages to your brain.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are right where you apply it — you may feel burning, stinging, warmth, or redness of the skin, especially at first. These feelings usually lessen the more you use it. Your eyes may water if you accidentally touch your face after applying it, so always wash your hands thoroughly after use.
warnings: Do not use this product on broken, irritated, or sunburned skin. Never apply it near your eyes, mouth, or private areas. Do not cover the treated area tightly with bandages or use a heating pad on top of it, as this can cause serious skin burns. Keep it away from children. If you develop severe skin irritation, blistering, or a rash, stop using it and contact your doctor. Do not use it before a bath or shower.
typical_dosing: For most adults, apply a small amount to the painful area up to 3 to 4 times a day, or as directed on the product label. Gently rub it into the skin until it is absorbed. Always wash your hands well after applying it. If you do not feel any improvement after a few weeks of regular use, talk to your doctor or pharmacist.
